sbg_auroc.notes: B08 (SBG) results_test.json stores auroc=0.423664. E6 h2_verdict rounds this to 0.4237 (4dp). round(0.423664, 4)==0.4237 confirmed. AUROC < 0.5 is correct: with threshold=1.000001 all pairs predicted CHANGED, and the inversion (SC mutations score higher than SP transforms) means lower-similarity ranks EQUIV first, giving sub-random discrimination.

best_baseline_auroc.notes: B02 (AST) results_test.json stores auroc=0.552845. E6 correctly identifies B02 as best baseline (highest AUROC in table). round(0.552845, 4)==0.5528 confirmed. B02 is above random (>0.5), but CI=[0.509, 0.593] overlaps 0.5, indicating marginal discrimination.

sbg_f1.notes: B08 threshold=1.000001 → all 744 pairs predicted CHANGED. tp=366, fp=378, fn=0, tn=0. F1 = 2*366/(2*366+378+0) = 732/1110 = 0.659459... confirmed. Same F1 as B02 and most other baselines because all use threshold=1.000001 and predict every pair as CHANGED.

inversion_delta.notes: E1 stores: SBG_static equiv_mean=0.9619, changed_mean=0.9954, delta=0.0335. Computed delta = round(0.9954 - 0.9619, 4) = 0.0335. Match confirmed. inversion=True because changed_mean > equiv_mean: CHANGED pairs score HIGHER than EQUIV. This is the structural-semantic inversion — SC mutations (off-by-one, operator swap) are near-identical syntactically, while SP transforms (refactoring) change structure. E2 stores identical values (changed_mean=0.9954, equiv_mean=0.9619), confirming consistency.

near_identical_fraction.notes: E2 stores near_identical_fraction_changed=0.9918 for SBG_static: 99.18% of CHANGED pairs (SC mutations) score >=0.99 similarity — nearly indistinguishable from identical code. Out of 366 CHANGED pairs, ~363 appear near-identical. Per-mutation breakdown shows SC-1/SC-3/SC-5/SC-9/SC-11 at fraction=1.0 (all instances look identical). Only SC-7 shows lower fraction (0.5), pulling the overall average below 1.0. No arithmetic inconsistency found.

mcnemar_p.notes: E6 stores: b=0, c=0, statistic=0.0, p_value=1.0. B08 and B02 BOTH use threshold=1.000001 → both predict EVERY pair as CHANGED. Therefore they agree on every single prediction: disagreements b=c=0. With b+c=0 the McNemar test has no valid statistic; p=1.0 is the standard convention (maximum non-significance). This is mathematically correct and well-documented in E6 note field: 'b+c=0 — classifiers agree on all disagreements'. VERIFIED.

e3_permutation_p.notes: H3 tests whether var(SC) > var(SP) — i.e., SBG is MORE stable under SP transforms. All three methods show the OPPOSITE: SP_std > SC_std in all cases. SBG_static: SP_std=0.05954, SC_std=0.00929; var_diff(SC-SP)=-0.003459 (negative). AST: SP_std=0.14046, SC_std=0.05339; var_diff=-0.016879 (negative). Token: SP_std=0.0508, SC_std=0.02324; var_diff=-0.00204 (negative). In a one-sided permutation test where H3 requires var(SC)-var(SP) > 0, an observed value of -0.003459 means ZERO permutations out of 1000 will exceed a negative observed value (all permutation diffs can be >=0 or negative, but the sign test means no permutation can 'beat' the negative observed). Therefore p=1.0 is correct: there is NO evidence for H3. Computed var differences match stored values within floating-point rounding. VERIFIED.

test_split_composition.notes: B02, B08, and E6 all store n_samples/n_test_pairs=744. E1 and E2 store n_equiv_pairs=378, n_changed_pairs=366 (378+366=744). Confirmed: 378 EQUIV + 366 CHANGED = 744 total test pairs. Split is slightly unbalanced (50.8% EQUIV vs 49.2% CHANGED) — random baseline would be ~50.8% accuracy, consistent with observed metrics. Seeds: all 42 as required.

b02_score_fn_spot_check.notes: score_fn independently executed on first 5 test pairs. All scores in [0,1]. SP-2 (rename variables) yields score=1.0 after normalization — correct because B02 normalizes variable names, so renamed vars look identical. SP-3 (algorithm restructure) yields scores 0.40-0.47 — correct because AST sequence changes substantially. These EQUIV pairs receiving LOW scores (0.40) directly confirm the inversion: the model assigns LOW similarity to EQUIV-restructured code, while SC mutations (near-identical AST) score ~1.0. AUROC formula and score_fn verified.

issues_found.description: E6 headline sbg_auroc=0.4237 is a 4dp rounded value of 0.423664 (B08). The rounding is correct (round-half-even at 4dp gives 0.4237). Not an error, but downstream citations should use 0.4237 (4dp) consistently.

McNemar p=1.0 arises because B08 and B02 share the same threshold=1.000001 and thus make identical predictions (all CHANGED). The McNemar test is therefore degenerate (b+c=0). This is a consequence of the threshold selection, not a bug. Any meaningful paired comparison of B02 vs B08 discrimination must use AUROC (which does differ: 0.5528 vs 0.4237), not the McNemar test.

E3 permutation p=1.0 for H3 ('SBG is more stable') is correct but could be misread as 'p=1.0 therefore strong evidence'. The correct interpretation is the opposite: p=1.0 means ZERO evidence for H3 (observed difference is in the WRONG direction). The artifact interpretation string correctly says 'NOT SUPPORTED'.

SP-3 EQUIV pairs receive B02 scores of 0.40-0.47 (very low similarity), confirming the inversion is real: AST sequence changes substantially under algorithm restructure. This is expected behavior for the benchmark design, but means B02 actively misclassifies SP-3 EQUIV pairs as CHANGED.

summary: All 6 headline metrics and the 2 statistical test results independently verified. B08 AUROC=0.4237 confirmed (B08 results_test.json stores 0.423664, rounds to 0.4237). B02 AUROC=0.5528 confirmed (B02 results_test.json stores 0.552845, rounds to 0.5528). Inversion delta=0.0335 arithmetic confirmed. Near-identical fraction=0.9918 confirmed. McNemar p=1.0 correct (b+c=0, degenerate test). E3 permutation p=1.0 correct (observed var diff is negative, cannot be exceeded). Score function live-tested on 5 pairs: all in [0,1], behavior consistent with inversion. No fabricated or incorrect numbers found in v1 artifacts. 4 informational notes recorded (rounding, degenerate McNemar, p-value interpretation, SP-3 behavior).
